solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City is very English, previously hazardous

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English
an obsolete sense of this word was precarious or risky, which 'previously' flags

explanation.surface: A traveller warns that some city is very English but was once a dangerous place.
explanation.walkthrough: VENICE: 'nice' once meant delicate or precarious, a sense still heard in 'a nice point'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon port of canals and gondolas is a famous city.

clue.text: Stalin and his sort see impedance in dosh being dished out

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: one symbol is placed inside the scrambled cash word
money dished out is scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: slang for money
Z is the physics symbol for electrical impedance

explanation.surface: A rant about Stalin's kind of tyrant spending ill-gotten cash freely.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes first; then Z sits among the jumbled letters of dosh to give VOZHDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vozhd is a Russian word for a supreme leader, the title applied to Stalin, so his sort are vozhds.

clue.text: Very bad rash showing under neon

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part sitting below another follows it in reading order

parts.note: Ne is the chemical symbol for neon
fast can mean reckless or dissipated

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a nasty rash appearing beneath a neon light.
explanation.walkthrough: NE above FAST gives NEFAST, a rare word from the Latin nefastus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefast is an archaic adjective meaning wicked or abominable, so extremely bad.

clue.text: Passion redolent of dark films number neglected

indicators.note: something neglected is left out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: suggestive of film noir, the shadowy crime-movie genre
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A critic finds passion in moody black-and-white cinema, though one count is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: NOIRISH loses NO to leave IRISH; 'to get one's Irish up' means to lose one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives Irish as an informal word for temper or a fit of anger, a kind of passion.

clue.text: Features of westerns in cinematographic action

indicators.note: the answer is found sitting within the next words of the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Film critics noting what makes westerns: the action and its photography.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites gunfights or saloons; the hidden word is the desert plants that dot every western backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Prickly desert plants are stock scenery in cowboy films set in the American south-west.

clue.text: Pulpit in what's central for keenest understanding

indicators.note: the pulpit word is placed inside the selected letters
only the middle portion of the following word is kept

parts.note: the three central letters of the seven
in Scotland a tent is a portable open-air pulpit for field preaching

explanation.surface: A preacher in the pulpit talks about the heart of keenest understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots field pulpit is a convention worth knowing: open-air communion services were preached from a wooden stand called a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an agreement or friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Tramp across Oz with it going on your toes mostly?

indicators.note: the pronoun departs from the word before it, so those letters are removed
only most of the phrase's word is used, its last letter dropped
one part is placed after, as if resting on, the other

parts.note: the word with, minus the letters of it
on your toes means alert; mostly loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A question about an Australian vagrant who keeps walking on tiptoe.
explanation.walkthrough: WITH loses IT to leave WH; ALERT loses its T. In Australian slang a whaler is a swagman who wanders along rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Whaler is old Australian slang for a tramp or swagman, someone wandering the outback with a swag.

clue.text: Antique stuffed into college bag

indicators.note: one thing is packed inside another, as stuffing goes into a case

parts.note: a hall is a college or a students' residence
something antique is old

explanation.surface: An old curio crammed into a student's college bag.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a hall is a college, or a residence for students.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag that carries everything.

clue.text: Motor blasted with leaves — not silent

parts.note: a German make of car

indicators.note: the abbreviation departs from the word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: blew is the past tense of blow, as a gale blasted
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A car caught in a gale is pelted with blown leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: AUDI plus BLEW without its W gives AUDIBLE. 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb of departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something audible can be heard, the opposite of making no sound at all.

clue.text: Possibly redden seeing a nun dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blushes at the sight of a nun dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shows the definition is an example: staining with blood is one way to redden.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensanguine is to stain or cover with blood, which colours a thing red.

clue.text: Slightly damaged paper put in box or similar again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a paper-trade term for second-quality sheets with small flaws

definitions.text: put in box or similar again
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to place on a tree again, box being a kind of tree

explanation.walkthrough: Box here is the evergreen shrub or tree, not a container, so the second meaning is to tree again.
explanation.definitionFit: Retree is paper slightly damaged in making, from French retrait; read as re-tree it means place back on a tree.

clue.text: We're done! Old TV recorder departs carried by Highland cattle

indicators.note: something carried is held inside its bearer

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
VERA was the BBC's early Vision Electronic Recording Apparatus
a Scots word for cattle, a variant of nowt
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A broadcaster signs off as an old video machine leaves on the backs of Highland cows.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the departs abbreviation is carried inside the cattle word; the old and recorder pieces simply stand before it. Highland flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Over and out is the radio operator's sign-off phrase meaning the exchange is finished.

clue.text: Ape's snarling snout? A weapon of doubtful destruction!

indicators.note: snarling suggests the letters are tangled up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
hooter is slang for the nose

explanation.surface: An angry ape bares its snout, but it is hardly a dangerous arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition parodies 'weapon of mass destruction' to describe a child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a small tube for blowing dried peas, a toy that does almost no harm.

clue.text: Let's do party for first-born?

indicators.note: letters that party go wild and end up in disorder

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A cheerful call to throw a celebration for the eldest child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-born child of a family is the eldest, born before all siblings.

clue.text: While inside breaking these old vows

indicators.note: the conjunction word goes within the other letters
something broken is smashed apart and its pieces rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
as can mean while, at the same time that

explanation.surface: Someone breaking their vows while on the inside, perhaps in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: AS goes inside a jumble of these. Heastes is Spenser's plural of hest, a behest or vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hest is an archaic word for a command or promise, and Spenser spelt its plural this way.

clue.text: Bit of dough belonging to Arab?

definitions.text: Bit of dough belonging to Arab?

indicators.note: only a small part, the opening letter, of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a thing belonging to a set is in it
Ar. is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A question about a piece of money owned by an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a dinar is a coin of several Arab countries, and dough is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency unit of Arab countries such as Jordan, Kuwait and Iraq.

clue.text: Stylish tip in German

parts.note: in West African English a dash is a tip or gratuity
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: a hint picked up in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it is simply part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing person is smart and stylish in dress and manner, with flair.

clue.text: One at sea with Macron's one over in Scotland

parts.note: an able-bodied seaman
the French for one, as the French president would say it

explanation.surface: A sailor and the French president share something above the Scottish border.
explanation.walkthrough: Abune is Scots for above, as in Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Abune is the Scots form of above, so it means over in Scottish dialect.

clue.text: Inspiring goddess before Tuesday put up with eccentricity

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: the Latin prefix for before
the abbreviation for Tuesday
e is the mathematical symbol for eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: A goddess turns up early on Tuesday and tolerates odd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but it splits: 'put up' turns the first pieces, and 'with' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is the Muse of music and lyric poetry, one of the goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Before noon girl gives you mushroom

parts.note: a.m. means ante meridiem, before noon
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl hands someone a mushroom in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is the genus of toadstools that includes the fly agaric and death cap.

clue.text: Get upset about urn payment to go

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the vessel word
upset letters are knocked over and end up rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an olla is an earthenware pot or jar

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry over the cost of a tea urn.
explanation.walkthrough: The olla is a Spanish earthenware pot; the jumbled letters split around it rather than sitting together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tollage is a toll or fee charged for passage along a road, over a bridge, or through a gate.

clue.text: Cut in dental examination going round

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: oral means of the mouth, like dental, and an oral is a spoken exam
a cut is a share or portion, a bit

explanation.surface: A dentist makes an incision during a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dental examination' reads as one phrase, but serves as a single clue to a word meaning both of the mouth and a spoken test.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital describes going round in an orbit, as a satellite circles a planet.

clue.text: Farm building church — America gets united within

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: the country word receives the next letter inside it

parts.note: Amer. is an abbreviation for America
U is the abbreviation for united

explanation.surface: A farm building serving as a church draws a united American congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaumer is a Scots form of chamber, the farm workers' sleeping quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a chaumer is a room on a farm where farm labourers slept, a bothy-like outbuilding.

clue.text: Thrawn? For limmers slate's on hold

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part sitting on another comes first

parts.note: cam is a Scots word for the soft white stone used for marking and whitening, the stuff of Scots rogues' slates
ho is an old word for a stop or halt

explanation.surface: A cryptic Scots-flavoured clue about rascals keeping their slate waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Limmers are Scots rogues, flagging a Scots word; camsho, also camshaugh, means crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrawn is Scots for twisted or perverse, and camsho is a Scots word for crooked or awry.

clue.text: Eastern noble's place one beset by raid

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides

parts.note: a do is slang for a raid or swindle
to aim is to direct or place a shot
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Japanese aristocrat's estate is attacked in a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Eastern noble is'. A do is British slang for a swindle or police raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A daimio was a Japanese feudal lord, a noble of the East under the shogun.

clue.text: Lumps of metal bought in angles

indicators.note: the purchase word is placed inside the other word

parts.note: an in is an angle, a way of getting access or influence
to have got something is to have obtained or bought it

explanation.surface: Bars of metal bought at a geometric angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angles' looks geometric, but it means routes to advantage, as in having an in with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are cast blocks of metal such as gold or steel.

clue.text: Archimedes' capital fragment about vessel

indicators.note: capital means head, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the initial letter of the name
an ort is a scrap or leftover fragment of food
a is an abbreviation for about, from Latin ante or circa usage in dates

explanation.surface: A scrap of a manuscript by Archimedes concerns a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is the blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Pass a black spot

parts.note: taken as written
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: A card player declines to bid, leaving a dark mark on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' means to decline a turn, as in a card game or a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from voting or taking part, to decline one's turn.

clue.text: Inclined to be careless with one opener out of place

indicators.note: the chosen letter is taken out of the careless word

parts.note: slapdash and untidy

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so the first letter of the last word

parts.note: the initial letter

explanation.surface: Someone tends to be slapdash when things are out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOPPY has two Ps; only one is removed, as 'one' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Slopy is an old form of sloping, so it means slanted or inclined.

clue.text: Endless twaddle about satisfactory punishments

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the approval word, which also turns round
the last letter of the nonsense word is cut off

parts.note: tosh is nonsense
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Endless nonsense about acceptable penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double work here: the approval word turns round as well as being enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Toko, or toco, is old slang for punishment or a thrashing, so tokos are punishments.

clue.text: May must no more turn to amongst chaps

indicators.note: one thing amongst others is placed within them

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: turning the short word reads it backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone may no longer be compelled to mix among the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No more' marks the definition as obsolete: moten is an old plural form of mote, meaning may or must.
explanation.definitionFit: Mote is an archaic verb meaning may or must, and moten is its old plural form.

clue.text: Pipe carrying crude oil for storing in towers

indicators.note: the pipe word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice

indicators.note: something crude is unrefined, so the letters are in rough disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pipeline carries crude oil for storage in tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' and 'crude oil' paint an oil pipeline, but pipe is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Siloing is putting grain or fodder into silos, the tall storage towers on farms.

clue.text: Concerned with layout of tiny things in stone — fine

definitions.text: Concerned with layout of tiny things

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
an eric was a fine paid for murder under old Irish law

explanation.surface: Arranging tiny objects inside a stone, done finely.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is 14 pounds in British weights.
explanation.definitionFit: Steric relates to the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule, the layout of minute particles.

clue.text: Plastic put on patio in part

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Plastic furniture set out on part of the patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' reads as garden furniture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to a point means partly or to some extent, but not completely.

clue.text: Moving away from original I put away syrup

indicators.note: the letter departs from the word, leaving it shorter

parts.note: orig. is the abbreviation for original
taken as written
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning an original idea and storing a bottle of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: ORIG without I gives ORG; add EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgeat is a sweet syrup flavoured with almonds and orange-flower water, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Cleaners left unknown solutions

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
y is an algebraic unknown
a sol is a colloidal solution

explanation.surface: Cleaning products leaving behind mysterious liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysol is a proprietary disinfectant used as a household cleaning product.
